subject: SignalPath migration: pricing parity ask and staged transition plan
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@signalpath.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: SignalPath Procurement <procurement@signalpath.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor comparison: parity request + migration tempo

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a quick internal econ model and the finance/ops team are asking whether Redwood can match pricing (or come within 8–10%) of our incumbent for the first 12 months given migration risk.

A few things they care about:
- Unit token price for embeddings and generation at our 800M monthly token baseline
- Any committed minimums or seat-based SKUs required for the discount
- Migration credits or onboarding support to offset integration effort

Would you be able to put together a short parity proposal with a staged transition plan (pilot > rollout) and any tradeoffs we should expect on latency/throughput? I attached our high-level usage export — happy to redact anything if you need more detail.

Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform Operations, SignalPath
elena.park@signalpath.com

Attachment: usage_export_aug2026.csv (csv)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@signalpath.com>
Cc: Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor comparison: parity request + migration tempo

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the context and the export. We can absolutely put together a parity-oriented offer; wanted to outline a recommended structure first so expectations are aligned:

1) Pricing construct
- Staged unit pricing: pilot (month 1–2) with a small pilot discount, ramped committed tier for months 3–12 with an invoice credit smoothing in months 3–6 if baseline usage meets projections.
- We typically avoid absolute price-matching guarantees because our runtime economics differ (batching, KV caching). Instead we offer an effective unit-cost match via credits + committed tiers.

2) Migration economics
- One-time onboarding credit (applied against first 3 invoices) to offset engineer time.
- Free technical migration sprints: two 4-hr workshops (architecture + ops handoff) and a concierge runbook from Grace's team.

3) Ops guarantees and fallbacks
- Canary rollout plan (5%, 25%, 100%) with automatic fallback to incumbent during early-stage regressions for first 30 days.
- Observability handoff: token-level cost/latency dashboards and a 90-day regression watch.

If that approach sounds reasonable I’ll work up a numerically explicit proposal (with token-price-equivalent, committed tier thresholds, and exact credit amounts). Grace — can you draft a migration checklist and estimate the typical eng hours for a SignalPath-scale integration so I can convert to a dollar credit?

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena.park@signalpath.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor comparison: parity request + migration tempo

Elena / Marcus —

Quick technical estimate and migration checklist attached. High‑level: for SignalPath’s profile (3 model endpoints, ~800M tokens/mo, latency SLO 150–200ms P95) we estimate 3 full‑time equivalent engineering days across 2 sprints for baseline integration and 6–8 days of ops-runbook and performance tuning during pilot.

Suggested credits to reflect that work:
- Onboarding credit: $18,000 applied across months 1–3 (covers 6–8 eng days + ops tuning).
- Pilot credit: $3,000 if pilot falls below the projected 60% usage threshold (to reduce risk).

We also recommend the following packaging:
- Month 1–2: Pilot tier — no long-term commit, reduced per-token pilot price (5% below list) and free tuning sprints.
- Months 3–12: Committed tier — 12% discount over list at 80% of projected baseline, plus the onboarding credit applied as invoice credit across months 1–3.

Caveat: if SignalPath requires an absolute price-match clause to a named incumbent in the contract, legal will need to tighten liability clauses; we usually achieve the economics via credits + guaranteed performance metrics instead of strict match language.

Attachment: redwood-migration-checklist.pdf (pdf)

Grace Oconnor
Director, Customer Reliability
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

From: Elena Park <elena.park@signalpath.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: SignalPath Procurement <procurement@signalpath.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor comparison: parity request + migration tempo

Thanks Marcus and Grace — this is helpful and close to what procurement was hoping to see. A couple quick clarifications before I take this to the budget committee: 

- Can you convert the committed‑tier discount and credits into an "effective per-token" number for both embeddings and text gen so we can line-item against our incumbent spreadsheet? (We track embeddings separately — about 200M tokens/mo.)
- Procurement would like the onboarding credit locked in the MSA as a dollar credit and the pilot credit to be applied automatically if pilot usage <60% without manual disputes.

I attached a first-pass SOW that our legal team prefers to start from — will you and Karthik review redlines? If we can get an effective per‑token comparison and confirm the credit mechanics, I can escalate to execs this week.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

Elena
Attachment: SignalPath_SOW_v1.docx (docx)
